clue.text: Fielder booted for being slovenly

parts.note: a slip is a cricket fielder stationed beside the wicketkeeper
booted means wearing footwear, i.e. shod

explanation.surface: A cricketer is dropped from the side for a sloppy display in the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Booted' suggests being kicked out of the team, but here it simply means wearing shoes. SLIP is a cricket fielding position close behind the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe work done carelessly and without attention to neatness.

clue.text: Very light-weight element one found in an Oxford classical school

indicators.note: found in means the numeral letter is placed inside the course name

parts.note: Lit. Hum. (Literae Humaniores) is the Oxford University degree course in classics
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A featherweight scholar turns up among Oxford's classicists.
explanation.walkthrough: LIT HUM is short for Literae Humaniores, the name of Oxford's classics degree.
explanation.definitionFit: The lightest metal in the periodic table, atomic number three.

clue.text: Set just above sea-level, barometer gives the full picture

parts.note: a pier is a structure standing just above the sea
glass is an old name for a barometer, as in 'the glass is falling'

explanation.surface: A weather forecast: being near sea level, the barometer gives a complete reading.
explanation.walkthrough: A pier glass is a tall mirror between windows, so it shows a full-length picture of whoever stands before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall wall mirror reflects a person head to toe, a complete image.

clue.text: Punishment when first caught would be a scolding

indicators.note: when first says the letter for caught would sit at the front, so it is removed from there

parts.note: chiding is another word for a scolding or telling-off
c is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A beating is what a reprimand becomes after a first offence is caught.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says the answer, with C (caught) placed first, would be CHIDING, a scolding; so remove that C.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrashing or beating, as in being given a good hiding.

clue.text: Dark room where industry is encouraged?

definitions.meaning: a photographic darkroom is where film is developed
a British region designated for government help to attract new businesses

explanation.surface: Asking whether a photographer's darkroom is a place where hard work is fostered.
explanation.walkthrough: A development area was a region of high unemployment where the UK government offered incentives for new industry.
explanation.definitionFit: A darkroom is literally a place for developing film, and the official term names regions given aid to attract factories.

clue.text: Ships' hooters sailors should ignore

definitions.meaning: the loud warning horns sounded by vessels
the singing nymphs of Greek myth who lured passing mariners onto the rocks

explanation.surface: Advice to seamen to pay no attention to the horns of other vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: Warning horns on boats share their name with the mythical singers whose song wrecked seafarers, as Odysseus knew.

clue.text: Turned out best, these Christmas trees, in every detail

parts.note: spruces are the conifers traditionally used as Christmas trees
to a T means exactly, in every detail

explanation.surface: The most perfectly decorated Christmas trees, finished in every detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned out best' means most smartly dressed. 'To a T' means perfectly, giving T.
explanation.definitionFit: Spruce means neat and smart in dress, so the superlative describes the smartest appearance.

clue.text: Cover that can be lowered over the organ

definitions.text: Cover that can be lowered over the organ

parts.words: Cover that can be lowered over the organ
parts.note: read the organ as a body part for hearing rather than a church instrument: a flap on a cap folding down over it

explanation.surface: A dust sheet let down over a church organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' suggests the musical instrument, but it is the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: A hat's side flap folds down to keep the ear warm.

clue.text: We're small, perhaps, for Dickensian boots

indicators.note: perhaps means the words we're small may be presented in another order

explanation.surface: Small people asking for footwear in the style of Dickens's era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boots' was the name for a hotel servant who cleaned shoes; Sam Weller is the boots at the White Hart inn in The Pickwick Papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Pickwick's servant first appears as the shoe-cleaner at a London inn in Dickens's first novel.

clue.text: Listen at first to nurse

indicators.note: first tells us the word at is placed before the other piece

parts.note: to nurse a patient is to tend them

explanation.surface: An instruction to pay attention to the nurse before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: To give heed or pay attention, as in attending to a speaker.

clue.text: Scholar's notebook

parts.note: read as a book full of notes by scholars: an edition of a text carrying the commentary of many different editors

explanation.surface: A student's jotter.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a pupil's exercise book; the cryptic reading is a book of notes compiled from various scholars.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin-derived term for an edition printed with the comments of various editors and commentators.

clue.text: Instrument in original condition

definitions.meaning: an early keyboard instrument, a small harpsichord popular in Tudor England

explanation.surface: An antique musical instrument still in mint condition.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a small Elizabethan harpsichord and also means pure or untouched, like virgin snow.

clue.text: Composure that is a help in the Orient

parts.note: keeping one's cool means keeping one's composure
i.e., abbreviation of id est, means that is

explanation.surface: Keeping calm is a useful quality when travelling in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: An old, now offensive, term for a hired labourer or porter in Asia.

clue.text: Dirty film label

definitions.meaning: a thin layer spread on a surface, as on a microscope slide
to brand someone falsely, to slander

explanation.surface: A tag stuck on a pornographic movie.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers soiling something, a thin layer such as a cervical test sample, and a slur attached to a person's name.

clue.text: Dressing table lighter?

parts.note: reading dressing as a sauce and lighter as a barge: a vessel carrying dressing on the dinner table

explanation.surface: A bedroom dressing table made of lighter wood.
explanation.walkthrough: A lighter is a flat-bottomed barge, so this is a 'boat' carrying sauce on the table.
explanation.definitionFit: A gravy jug shaped like a little ship holds sauce at the table.

clue.text: Kind of special post office belonging to the bishops

indicators.note: kind of suggests a loose version of the following words, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A church-run mail service set aside for its clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of' rearranges SPECIAL together with PO to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes church government by, or relating to, bishops.

clue.text: It makes an extra space between lines — one per rod, perhaps

definitions.text: It makes an extra space between lines

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the words one per rod could appear in another arrangement

explanation.surface: Measuring spacing in a field: one marker for each rod of distance.
explanation.walkthrough: A rod is an old unit of length; the answer is a military formation in which soldiers stand with wider gaps between ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill formation with wider intervals between the ranks of troops.

clue.text: Selling on credit, he carries a name-tag

definitions.text: Selling on credit, he carries a name-tag

parts.words: Selling on credit, he carries a name-tag
parts.note: a man with a tally, the stick or account recording what customers owe, who sells goods on hire purchase

explanation.surface: A credit salesman wears an ID badge.
explanation.walkthrough: A tally was a notched stick or record of debts; the man who kept one sold goods on weekly instalments.
explanation.definitionFit: A door-to-door trader who sells goods for weekly payments, keeping an account of each debt.

clue.text: Not apologising for a fake in nude form

indicators.note: in tells us one group of letters goes inside the other
form means the word nude is given a new shape, its letters reshuffled

parts.note: a sham is a fake or fraud

explanation.surface: A naked impostor shows no remorse about the deception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fake' looks like part of the surface story of a naked impostor, but here it simply means a sham; 'form' is the anagram signal working on the word nude.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without shame offers no apology for what they have done.

clue.text: Recklessness of fellow propping up a bar

indicators.note: in a down clue the propping piece sits beneath the rest, so it comes last

parts.note: to bar is to ban, and a ban is a bar
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: Drunken behaviour of a man leaning on a pub counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub, but it means a prohibition, BAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild abandon means a complete lack of restraint.

clue.text: It's like a monkey with a bird in each hand

indicators.note: in shows the bird sits between the two hand letters

parts.note: L and R stand for left and right, one letter for each hand
the emu is a large flightless Australian bird

explanation.surface: A primate pictured clutching a bird in both fists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Each hand' gives both L (left) and R (right), and the bird goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: This Madagascan primate resembles a monkey but belongs to a separate group, the prosimians.

clue.text: British eel pie the French find stringy object

parts.note: UK is the abbreviation for the United Kingdom

indicators.note: pie is printers' term for type jumbled together, so it scrambles the word eel

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: French diners find a jellied eel pie from Britain full of stringy bits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pie' looks like food but means jumbled; it turns EEL into ELE.
explanation.definitionFit: A small four-stringed guitar from Hawaii, an object fitted with strings.

clue.text: Makes dirty form of rhyme in G and S

indicators.note: in shows the verse word sits between the two letters

parts.note: the letters G and S as given
rime is an old spelling of rhyme

explanation.surface: Grubbing up a type of verse in Gilbert and Sullivan.
explanation.walkthrough: G and S suggests Gilbert and Sullivan, but it simply supplies the two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To begrime something is to soil it with grime.

clue.text: Ornament to put on a hard surface

definitions.meaning: to decorate with a glassy coating

definitions.text: to put on a hard surface
definitions.meaning: to coat with a hard glossy finish, as on a bath or cooking pot

explanation.surface: Decorating with a glazed coating.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to decorate with vitreous glaze and to coat something with a hard glossy paint.

clue.text: Total sales, in the case of pastry

definitions.meaning: a firm's gross revenue over a period
a folded pastry case with a fruit filling

explanation.surface: A baker's sales figures for his pies.
explanation.definitionFit: Business revenue shares its name with a folded pastry such as an apple puff.

clue.text: Veteran hunter, for example

definitions.meaning: someone long experienced in an activity
a hunter is a pocket watch with a hinged cover, so an antique timepiece

explanation.surface: An experienced huntsman as the model of a seasoned old hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hunter' looks like someone who hunts, but it is a type of pocket watch with a protective lid, making it an old timepiece.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-serving person is an old hand, and an antique watch is literally an aged timekeeper.

clue.text: Perhaps minded to refuse

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the word minded is only one possible arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Someone might be inclined to say no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb (decline), but it is the noun meaning rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A heap of household waste or dung is a dunghill of rubbish.

clue.text: Fasten donkey's middle with a cord

indicators.note: middle points to the letters lying in the centre of the words fasten donkey's

explanation.surface: Instructions to tie a rope around a donkey's waist.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong fibrous band joining muscle to bone, sometimes called a sinew or cord.

clue.text: One who sucks up may get a shock on the road

definitions.meaning: something or someone that soaks up, like a sponge

definitions.text: may get a shock on the road
definitions.meaning: a shock ... takes jolts from the road surface in a car's suspension

explanation.surface: A creep who toadies to the boss may be in for a nasty surprise while driving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sucks up' suggests flattery, but it means soaking up; the second part completes a car's shock absorber.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything that soaks up liquid or energy takes it in, and a car's damper takes in bumps.
